title: Yoneda splicing respects equivalence and annihilates a zero prefix
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A degree-$r$ Yoneda extension of $U$ by $V$, for $r\geq1$, means an exact sequence $0\to V\to X_{r-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\to U\to0$. Equivalence means the relation generated by morphisms of these sequences fixing both endpoints. Fix a short exact sequence $\sigma:0\to K\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{q}F\to0$ and an integer $m\geq1$. For an $m$-extension $\eta:0\to T\to X_{m-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\xrightarrow{d}K\to0$, its splice with $\sigma$ is the exact $(m+1)$-extension $0\to T\to X_{m-1}\to\cdots\to X_0\xrightarrow{i\circ d}P\xrightarrow{q}F\to0$. Splicing with $\sigma$ preserves Yoneda equivalence. If $\eta$ is Yoneda equivalent to the zero $m$-extension of $K$ by $T$, its splice is Yoneda equivalent to the zero $(m+1)$-extension of $F$ by $T$. Here the zero $1$-extension is $0\to T\to T\oplus K\to K\to0$ with the standard inclusion and projection. For $r\geq2$, the zero $r$-extension of $U$ by $V$ has first middle object $V$, last middle object $U$, $r-2$ intervening zero objects, identity arrows at the endpoints, and zero arrows between middle objects. No projective or injective objects are assumed.

proof.text: The specified zero extensions are exact. In degree one, the kernel of the projection $T\oplus K\to K$ is the standard inclusion of $T$, and the inclusion and projection are respectively monic and epic by their retractions and sections. For degree $r\geq2$, exactness at the first middle object follows from $\operatorname{im}(1_V)=V=\ker(0)$, and at the last from $\operatorname{im}(0)=0=\ker(1_U)$; at intervening zero objects both sides are zero. These calculations use the zero object and biproducts of the abelian category [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension) and Tag 06XP (section-ext), exact-sequence composition paragraph after lemma-ext-1; explicit elementary argument by Q03.

proof.text: Check that splicing produces an exact extension. The short exact tail makes $i$ monic, $q$ epic, and $i$ a kernel of $q$; the prefix makes $d$ epic. Since $i$ is monic, a map $a$ into $X_0$ satisfies $ida=0$ exactly when $da=0$, so the kernel at $X_0$ is unchanged. Since $d$ is epic, a map $b$ out of $P$ satisfies $bid=0$ exactly when $bi=0$. Thus the cokernels of $id$ and $i$ agree, and so do their images (the kernels of their cokernels in an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]); this image is $\ker q$. All other exactness conditions are unchanged from the prefix and tail. This also covers $m=1$, where the preceding arrow is $T\to X_0$.

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension) and Tag 06XP (section-ext), exact-sequence composition paragraph after lemma-ext-1; explicit elementary argument by Q03.

proof.text: Let $f:\eta\to\eta'$ be a morphism of $m$-extensions fixing $T$ and $K$, with middle components $f_j:X_j\to X'_j$. Keep these components and put the identity on $P$ and $F$. Every old square still commutes; the new joining square commutes because $d' f_0=d$ gives $i d'f_0=i d$, and the final square is $q1_P=1_Fq$. This is a morphism of the spliced extensions, fixing their endpoints. Apply this construction to each arrow, in its given direction, in a finite zigzag generating Yoneda equivalence. The resulting zigzag proves that splicing preserves the equivalence relation defined in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension) and Tag 06XP (section-ext), exact-sequence composition paragraph after lemma-ext-1; explicit elementary argument by Q03.

proof.text: For $m=1$, splice the specified zero prefix. The resulting exact sequence is $0\to T\xrightarrow{\iota_T}T\oplus K\xrightarrow{i\pi_K}P\xrightarrow{q}F\to0$. Map it to the zero $2$-extension $0\to T\xrightarrow{1_T}T\xrightarrow{0}F\xrightarrow{1_F}F\to0$, with identities on the endpoints, $\pi_T:T\oplus K\to T$, and $q:P\to F$. The three squares say $\pi_T\iota_T=1_T$, $q i\pi_K=0\pi_T=0$, and $1_Fq=q$. Thus this endpoint-fixing morphism witnesses the required equivalence. Only the biproduct identities from [def-sp-abelian] and $qi=0$ from the given short exact sequence are used.

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension) and Tag 06XP (section-ext), exact-sequence composition paragraph after lemma-ext-1; explicit elementary argument by Q03.

proof.text: For $m\geq2$, the splice of the zero prefix has $m+1$ middle objects: $T$, then $m-2$ zero objects, then $K$, then $P$. The target zero $(m+1)$-extension has middle objects $T$, then $m-1$ zero objects, then $F$. Define a morphism from the splice to this target by the identity on the first $T$, the unique maps between zero objects, the zero map $K\to0$, and $q:P\to F$, fixing the endpoints $T,F$. At the first endpoint the square is the identity; at $K\to P$ it is $qi=0$; at $P\to F$ it is $1_Fq=q$; all other squares involve zero arrows and commute. When $m=2$ there are no zero objects before $K$ in the source, and the first interior square is still $0=0$. This gives the required endpoint-fixing comparison in every $m\geq2$.

source.place: Tag 06XT (definition-yoneda-extension) and Tag 06XP (section-ext), exact-sequence composition paragraph after lemma-ext-1; explicit elementary argument by Q03.

proof.text: If $\eta$ is equivalent to its specified zero $m$-extension, step 3 gives a zigzag between their splices. Step 4 (if $m=1$) or step 5 (if $m\geq2$) appends one endpoint-fixing morphism from the splice of that zero prefix to the specified zero $(m+1)$-extension. Concatenating these zigzags proves the assertion. No projective or injective objects, derived Ext comparison, or additional hypotheses have been used.
